notes: This paper constrains the axion parameter space using neutron star cooling observations. The primary result is presented in Fig. 5 as an exclusion region in the (f_a, m_a) plane, shown as a bright red band. The exclusion arises from the formation of a new ground state (NGS) of nuclear matter when ϵ ≲ 0.1, which causes envelope thinning and anomalously fast cooling inconsistent with observed isolated neutron stars (particularly the 'magnificent seven'). The constraint is model-dependent on the parameter ϵ in the axion potential (Eq. 2), with ϵ = 1 being the standard QCD axion. The paper focuses on the regime where ϵ ≤ 1 (lighter axions than standard QCD prediction). The excluded region boundaries are: (1) right boundary at ϵ ≈ 0.1 where NGS disappears; (2) left boundary where NGS appears below the envelope base density ρ_b; (3) lower boundary where structural changes become insignificant. The data points provided represent approximate corners of the excluded region spanning f_a from ~10^12 to ~10^17 GeV and m_a from ~10^-20 to ~10^-5 eV, though the exact numerical boundaries depend on the ϵ parameter and are read from Fig. 5. Extraction confidence is moderate (0.65) because: (1) the coupling type is AxionMass (f_a vs m_a plane) which is correct for this cosmological/astrophysical bound, but (2) the exact numerical boundaries of the exclusion region in Fig. 5 are somewhat difficult to read precisely from the figure, and (3) the constraint is model-dependent on ϵ.
